subject: B
topic: Centrally Sponsored Schemes & Indian Foreign Trade

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which centrally sponsored scheme was launched in 2015 to provide life insurance coverage of ₹2 lakh at a premium of ₹12 per year to the poor and underprivileged sections of society?
options: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provides accidental death and disability insurance of ₹2 lakh at ₹12/year premium. PMJJBY is wrong because it provides life insurance at ₹330/year, not ₹12. Atal Pension Yojana is wrong because it is a pension scheme, not an insurance scheme. PMJDY is wrong because it is a financial inclusion scheme for opening bank accounts, not an insurance product.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):

(i) It guarantees 150 days of wage employment per year to every rural household.
(ii) It was enacted in 2005 and came into force in 2006.
(iii) Unemployment allowance must be paid if work is not provided within 15 days of application.
(iv) The wages under MGNREGA are linked to the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: MGNREGA was enacted in 2005 and came into force on 2 February 2006 (ii is correct). Unemployment allowance is payable if work is not provided within 15 days (iii is correct). Wages are indeed linked to CPI-AL (iv is correct). Statement (i) is wrong because MGNREGA guarantees 100 days, not 150 days, of wage employment per household per year.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's largest trading partner by total bilateral trade volume (imports + exports) in the financial year 2023-24 was:
questions.explanation: The USA became India's largest overall trading partner in FY 2023-24 by total bilateral trade volume. China is wrong because while it is the largest single source of imports, total bilateral trade (exports + imports combined) was slightly lower than the USA. UAE is wrong because although it is a major trade partner, its total volume is lower than the USA and China. Saudi Arabia is wrong because trade with it is dominated only by oil imports and total volume is much lower.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide 'Housing for All' by the year 2022.
Reason (R): Under PMAY-Gramin, beneficiaries in plain areas receive financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh for construction of houses.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — PMAY's stated target is Housing for All by 2022 (later extended). Reason (R) is also correct — under PMAY-Gramin, plain area beneficiaries receive ₹1.20 lakh. However, the financial assistance amount is a feature of the scheme's implementation, not the reason why the scheme aims for Housing for All — that aim stems from the policy objective of addressing the housing deficit. Hence (R) does not explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are items that India primarily exports?

(i) Petroleum products
(ii) Gems and jewellery
(iii) Crude petroleum
(iv) Information technology services

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: India is a major exporter of petroleum products (refined), gems and jewellery, and IT services — all three are among the top export categories. Crude petroleum (iii) is wrong because India is a net importer of crude oil; it imports about 85% of its crude oil requirements and does not figure among primary exports.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following centrally sponsored schemes with their primary objectives:

Column I:
(a) Swachh Bharat Mission
(b) Ayushman Bharat – PMJAY
(c) Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
(d) PM-KISAN

Column II:
(i) Direct income support to small and marginal farmers
(ii) Universal school education from pre-school to Class XII
(iii) Health insurance coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year
(iv) Elimination of open defecation and solid waste management

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Swachh Bharat Mission (a) focuses on elimination of open defecation (iv). Ayushman Bharat PMJAY (b) provides ₹5 lakh health insurance (iii). Samagra Shiksha (c) integrates school education from pre-school to XII (ii). PM-KISAN (d) provides income support to farmers (i). The second option is wrong because it wrongly assigns education to PMJAY. The third option is wrong because it assigns health insurance to Swachh Bharat. The fourth option is wrong because it assigns income support to Samagra Shiksha.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act in India was enacted in the year:
questions.explanation: The SEZ Act was passed by Parliament in May 2005 and came into effect in February 2006. 2003 is wrong because the SEZ policy existed under EXIM Policy then, but the formal Act had not yet been passed. 2000 is wrong because that was when India's first SEZ policy was introduced under the Export-Import Policy, not the Act. 2007 is wrong because by that year the Act was already operational and multiple SEZs had been notified.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and its impact on India's foreign trade:

(i) GST subsumed multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, and VAT.
(ii) Exports under GST are treated as zero-rated supplies.
(iii) GST is levied on imports as IGST, making imported goods costlier relative to domestic goods.
(iv) GST has no impact on the logistics cost of export consignments.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: GST subsumed excise, service tax, VAT, etc. (i is correct). Exports are zero-rated so exporters can claim full input tax credit (ii is correct). IGST is levied on imports in lieu of customs countervailing duty, making imports relatively costlier (iii is correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because GST actually reduced logistics costs by eliminating inter-state check posts and multiple tax documentation requirements.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), the maximum premium payable by farmers for Kharif food and oilseed crops is:
questions.explanation: Under PMFBY, farmers pay a maximum premium of 2% of the sum insured for Kharif crops. 1.5% is wrong because that is the premium cap for Rabi crops, not Kharif. 5% is wrong because that rate applies to annual commercial and horticultural crops. 3% is wrong because no such slab exists under PMFBY guidelines.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has consistently maintained a trade deficit in merchandise trade over the last two decades.
Reason (R): India's imports of crude oil, gold, and electronic goods substantially exceed its merchandise exports.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India has indeed had a persistent merchandise trade deficit (A is correct). The major reasons are heavy imports of crude oil, gold, and electronics which far exceed export revenues (R is correct). Since R directly explains why the deficit persists, R is the correct explanation of A. Option 2 is wrong because R does explain A. Option 3 is wrong because R is factually correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is also factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched in September 2014 primarily to boost which sector of the Indian economy?
questions.explanation: Make in India was launched to transform India into a global manufacturing hub and increase the share of manufacturing in GDP. Agricultural sector is wrong because schemes like PM-KISAN and PMFBY target agriculture. IT sector is wrong because it was already well-established through earlier policies like the IT Act. Service and hospitality sector is wrong because the initiative specifically targeted manufacturing and industrial production.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are objectives of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013?

(i) Provide subsidised foodgrains to approximately 75% of rural and 50% of urban population
(ii) Entitle priority households to 35 kg of foodgrains per month
(iii) Provide maternity benefit of ₹6,000 to pregnant women
(iv) Supply foodgrains at ₹1/kg for rice, ₹2/kg for wheat, and ₹3/kg for coarse grains

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: NFSA covers up to 75% rural and 50% urban population (i is correct). It provides maternity benefit of not less than ₹6,000 (iii is correct). Foodgrains are supplied at ₹3/2/1 per kg for rice/wheat/coarse grains (iv is correct). Statement (ii) is wrong because priority households under NFSA are entitled to 5 kg per person per month (not 35 kg per household — that was the old BPL entitlement under the Targeted PDS, not NFSA's general category).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian exports with their top destination countries (as of recent trade data):

Column I:
(a) Petroleum products
(b) IT and software services
(c) Cut and polished diamonds
(d) Basmati rice

Column II:
(i) United States of America
(ii) Saudi Arabia and UAE
(iii) Belgium and Hong Kong
(iv) Netherlands and Singapore

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: India exports petroleum products mainly to Netherlands and Singapore (a-iv). IT services are exported predominantly to the USA (b-i). Cut and polished diamonds go mainly to Belgium and Hong Kong (c-iii). Basmati rice is exported largely to Saudi Arabia and UAE (d-ii). Option 2 is wrong because it wrongly pairs petroleum with Saudi Arabia/UAE (they are oil exporters to India). Option 3 is wrong because diamonds don't primarily go to USA. Option 4 is wrong because it misassigns petroleum products.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Skill India Mission, launched in 2015, operates primarily through which nodal ministry?
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.correctAnswer: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The Skill India Mission is implemented by the dedicated Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) created in 2014. Ministry of HRD (now Education) is wrong because it deals with formal education, not vocational skilling. Ministry of Labour is wrong because while it handles employment statistics and labour laws, skill development has a separate ministry. Ministry of Commerce is wrong because it focuses on trade policy, not workforce skilling.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India's services exports have shown robust growth and help offset the merchandise trade deficit.
Reason (R): India is the world's largest exporter of iron ore and mineral resources.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India's IT, BPO, and professional services exports generate a large services surplus that partly offsets the merchandise trade deficit. Reason (R) is incorrect — India is NOT the world's largest exporter of iron ore (Australia and Brazil lead). Option 1 is wrong because R is factually false. Option 2 is wrong for the same reason. Option 4 is wrong because A is factually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) primarily aims to:
options: Organise rural poor women into Self-Help Groups and provide sustainable livelihood opportunities
Provide free LPG connections to Below Poverty Line rural households
Build rural road connectivity to unconnected habitations
Supply piped drinking water to every rural household by 2024
questions.correctAnswer: Organise rural poor women into Self-Help Groups and provide sustainable livelihood opportunities
questions.explanation: DAY-NRLM focuses on reducing poverty by enabling rural poor households (especially women) to access gainful self-employment through SHGs. Free LPG connections option is wrong because that is the objective of PM Ujjwala Yojana. Rural road connectivity option is wrong because that is the objective of PMGSY (Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana). Piped drinking water option is wrong because that is the objective of Jal Jeevan Mission.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's Balance of Payments:

(i) Current account includes trade in goods, services, and unilateral transfers.
(ii) Capital account records foreign direct investment and portfolio investment flows.
(iii) Remittances from Indians working abroad are recorded in the capital account.
(iv) A current account surplus means the country exports more than it imports in goods and services combined.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The current account includes trade in goods, services, income, and transfers (i is correct). The capital account records FDI and FPI flows (ii is correct). A current account surplus indicates net exports exceed net imports (iv is correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because remittances (private transfers) from abroad are recorded in the current account under 'secondary income/transfers', not the capital account.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which centrally sponsored scheme provides a __________ subsidy on the cost of installing solar rooftop systems for residential consumers under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana?
options: Up to 60% for the first 2 kW and 40% for the next 1 kW
Flat 50% for installations up to 5 kW capacity
Up to 30% for all installations regardless of capacity
Up to 75% for the first 1 kW and 25% for the next 2 kW
questions.correctAnswer: Up to 60% for the first 2 kW and 40% for the next 1 kW
questions.explanation: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, the central subsidy is 60% of the benchmark cost for the first 2 kW and 40% for the additional capacity up to 3 kW. Flat 50% is wrong because the subsidy is graded, not flat. 30% for all is wrong because the initial subsidy is much higher at 60%. 75% for 1 kW is wrong because no such slab exists in the scheme guidelines.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following trade-related organisations with their headquarters:

Column I:
(a) World Trade Organization (WTO)
(b) International Monetary Fund (IMF)
(c) Asian Development Bank (ADB)
(d) World Customs Organization (WCO)

Column II:
(i) Manila, Philippines
(ii) Washington D.C., USA
(iii) Geneva, Switzerland
(iv) Brussels, Belgium

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: WTO is headquartered in Geneva (a-iii). IMF is in Washington D.C. (b-ii). ADB is in Manila (c-i). WCO is in Brussels (d-iv). Option 2 is wrong because it places IMF in Manila. Option 3 is wrong because it places WTO in Brussels. Option 4 is wrong because it places ADB in Brussels and WCO in Manila.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY):

(i) It provides loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
(ii) Loans are categorised as Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
(iii) The scheme requires collateral for loans above ₹2 lakh.
(iv) It was launched in April 2015.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: PMMY provides collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh to micro enterprises (i is correct). The three categories Shishu, Kishore, Tarun are correctly described (ii is correct). It was launched on 8 April 2015 (iv is correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because MUDRA loans are collateral-free — no collateral is required at any level up to ₹10 lakh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: India's foreign trade policy (FTP) 2023, announced in March 2023, has no fixed end date. This is a departure from earlier policies because:
options: Earlier FTPs were valid for a fixed five-year period
Earlier FTPs were valid for a fixed three-year period
Earlier FTPs were renewed annually by Parliament
Earlier FTPs were permanent but amended every decade
questions.correctAnswer: Earlier FTPs were valid for a fixed five-year period
questions.explanation: India's earlier Foreign Trade Policies (e.g., FTP 2015-20) were announced for fixed five-year periods. The FTP 2023 is open-ended with periodic amendments. Three-year period is wrong because FTPs have traditionally been five-year documents. Annual renewal by Parliament is wrong because FTP is an executive policy, not a legislative act. Permanent with decadal amendments is wrong because the policy was always time-bound at five years.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are features of the Jal Jeevan Mission?

(i) It aims to provide functional household tap connections to every rural household by 2024
(ii) It is a centrally sponsored scheme with 90:10 Centre-State funding for Himalayan and NE states
(iii) Implementation is done through Gram Panchayats and local community participation
(iv) It covers only Below Poverty Line households in rural areas

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: JJM aims for functional household tap connections to every rural household (i is correct). The funding pattern is 90:10 for Himalayan/NE states (ii is correct). Gram Panchayats play a key role in planning and implementation (iii is correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because JJM is universal — it covers ALL rural households, not just BPL households.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) in international trade refers to:
options: A principle under WTO that requires a country to extend trade concessions equally to all member nations
A special bilateral treaty giving exclusive tariff benefits to one strategic ally
A UN Security Council designation granting veto power in trade disputes
A preferential status given only to developing nations under the Generalised System of Preferences
questions.correctAnswer: A principle under WTO that requires a country to extend trade concessions equally to all member nations
questions.explanation: MFN is a WTO principle (Article I of GATT) requiring non-discrimination — any advantage given to one member must be extended to all. The bilateral treaty option is wrong because MFN is multilateral, not exclusive to one ally. The UN Security Council option is wrong because MFN has nothing to do with the UNSC or veto power. The GSP option is wrong because GSP is a unilateral preferential scheme for developing countries, separate from MFN.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The data below shows India's merchandise trade (in US$ billion) for selected years:

2020-21: Exports 292, Imports 394
2021-22: Exports 422, Imports 613
2022-23: Exports 447, Imports 714
2023-24: Exports 437, Imports 677

In which year was the trade deficit (Imports minus Exports) the highest?
questions.explanation: Trade deficit: 2020-21 = 394-292 = $102B; 2021-22 = 613-422 = $191B; 2022-23 = 714-447 = $267B; 2023-24 = 677-437 = $240B. The highest deficit was $267 billion in 2022-23. 2021-22 is wrong because the deficit was $191B. 2023-24 is wrong because the deficit was $240B. 2020-21 is wrong because the deficit was only $102B.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Under the Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), what is the maximum health insurance coverage provided per family per year?
questions.explanation: AB-PMJAY provides cashless health insurance coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation. ₹3 lakh is wrong because that was the coverage under the earlier RSBY scheme. ₹7 lakh is wrong because no central health insurance scheme offers this amount. ₹10 lakh is wrong because PMJAY's ceiling is ₹5 lakh, not ₹10 lakh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The __________ is the apex body responsible for promoting India's exports by providing pre-shipment and post-shipment export credit guarantees to exporters and banks.
options: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC)
questions.correctAnswer: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC)
questions.explanation: ECGC provides credit risk insurance and guarantees to Indian exporters and banks against non-payment risks. EXIM Bank is wrong because it provides direct lending for exports/imports, not credit guarantee/insurance. DGFT is wrong because it is the regulatory body for trade policy and licensing, not credit guarantees. FIEO is wrong because it is a trade promotion body representing exporters, not a financial guarantee institution.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India initiative:

(i) It was launched on 16 January 2016.
(ii) Recognised startups get a three-year income tax exemption within the first ten years of incorporation.
(iii) The scheme provides automatic patent examination and an 80% rebate on patent filing fees.
(iv) Only technology companies can register under the Startup India scheme.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016 (i is correct). Eligible startups get 3 consecutive years of tax exemption out of first 10 years (ii is correct). Fast-tracked patent examination with 80% fee rebate is provided (iii is correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because startups from ANY sector — manufacturing, services, agriculture, social enterprise — can register; it is not limited to technology companies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The data below shows the share of various sectors in India's total exports for a recent financial year:

Petroleum Products: 18%, Gems & Jewellery: 9%, Pharmaceuticals: 7%, IT & Software Services: 23%, Textiles & Apparel: 6%, Engineering Goods: 14%, Others: 23%.

Which category has the second highest share among merchandise exports (excluding services)?
questions.explanation: Excluding services (IT & Software), the merchandise exports are: Petroleum Products 18%, Engineering Goods 14%, Gems & Jewellery 9%, Pharmaceuticals 7%, Textiles 6%. Engineering Goods at 14% is the second highest after Petroleum Products at 18%. Petroleum Products is wrong because it is the highest, not the second highest. Gems & Jewellery at 9% is third. Pharmaceuticals at 7% is fourth.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), the world's largest free trade agreement by GDP coverage?
questions.explanation: India withdrew from RCEP negotiations in November 2019 citing concerns about cheap Chinese imports harming domestic industries, and did not sign the agreement in 2020. China is wrong because it is a founding signatory of RCEP. Japan is wrong because it signed RCEP in November 2020. Australia is wrong because it also signed and ratified RCEP.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'One District One Product' (ODOP) programme, integrated with the Districts as Export Hubs initiative, aims to:
options: Identify and promote a specific product from each district for export potential and value addition
Restrict each district to manufacturing only one product to avoid competition
Provide free land to foreign companies for setting up one factory per district
Limit imports to only one category of goods per district to protect local industry
questions.correctAnswer: Identify and promote a specific product from each district for export potential and value addition
questions.explanation: ODOP identifies unique products with export potential from each district and promotes them through value addition, branding, and marketing support. The restriction option is wrong because ODOP promotes a focus product — it does not legally restrict other manufacturing. The free land option is wrong because the scheme has no provision for land grants to foreign companies. The import limitation option is wrong because ODOP is an export promotion initiative, not an import restriction mechanism.
